source_text: θεοῦ οἰκεῖ ἐν ὑμῖν;» καί· «οὐκ οἴδατε, ὅτι τὰ σώματα ὑμῶν ναὸς τοῦ ἐν ὑμῖν ἁγίου πνεύματός ἐστιν, οὗ ἔχετε ἀπὸ τοῦ θεοῦ;» 20.7 καὶ Ἐφεσίοις· «ἵνα δῴη ὑμῖν κατὰ τὸν πλοῦτον τῆς δόξης αὐτοῦ, δυνάμει κραταιωθῆναι διὰ τοῦ πνεύματος αὐτοῦ εἰς τὸν ἔσω ἄνθρωπον, κατοικῆσαι τὸν Χριστὸν διὰ τῆς πίστεως ἐν ταῖς καρδίαις ὑμῶν.» 20.8 Καὶ ὡς ὅταν ὁ δεσπότης ἐν Ἰωάννῃ λέγει· «τὸ πνεῦμα τῆς ἀληθείας, ὃ ὁ κόσμος οὐ δύναται λαβεῖν, ὅτι οὐ θεωρεῖ αὐτὸ οὐδὲ γινώσκει αὐτό. ὑμεῖς δὲ γινώσκετε αὐτό, ὅτι παρ' ὑμῖν μένει καὶ ἐν ὑμῖν ἔσται». καὶ πάλιν· «ἐάν τις ἀγαπᾷ με, τὸν λόγον μου τηρήσει· καὶ ὁ πατήρ μου ἀγαπήσει αὐτόν, καὶ πρὸς αὐτὸν ἐλευσόμεθα καὶ μονὴν παρ' αὐτῷ ποιησόμεθα». 20.9 Ἔσται δὲ τοῦτο πλέον καταφανὲς τῷ ἐπιστάνοντι, ὅτι θελήσας ὁ πάντα δυνάμενος θεὸς λόγος ἄτρεπτός τε διέμεινεν καὶ ὑπὸ τῆς παρθένου ἐκυοφορήθη. 20.10 Οἱ δὲ πάλιν ἐνίστανται ἀντιλέγοντες· «γέγραπται δῆθεν περὶ μὲν _̓Ανανία· «διὰ τί ἐπλήρωσεν ὁ σατανᾶς τὴν καρδίαν σου;» περὶ δὲ Ἰούδα, ὡς «εἰσῆλθεν εἰς αὐτὸν ὁ σατανᾶς».» 20.11 Πρὸς οὓς ῥητέον, ὡς οὐ μετεχόμενος οὐδὲ τῇ ψυχῇ ὥσπερ ἐπιβατεύων, ἀλλὰ φενακίζων καὶ κακοβουλίας καὶ παλίμβολον τρόπον ἐνεργαζόμενος καὶ πάρεργον ποιῶν τῆς ἑαυτοῦ πονηρίας πληροῖ τὸν μὴ προσέχοντα τῷ. «μὴ δῴης εἰς σάλον τὸν πόδα σου, καὶ οὐ μὴ νυστάξει ὁ φυλάσσων σε». 20.12 καθ' ὃν τρόπον Ἔλυμαν τὸν υἱὸν αὐτοῦ ἐπλήρωσεν τῇ ὑποβολῇ πράξεως σατανικῆς. λέγει γὰρ αὐτῷ Παῦλος, μυσαρῷ τὴν γνώμην καὶ τὰς πράξεις τυγχάνοντι καὶ ἀνάπλεῳ τῆς διαβολικῆς ὄντι μοχθηρίας καὶ κατασοφιζομένῳ τοὺς ἁγίους, ὡς δοκεῖν ἐν αὐτῷ οἰκεῖν τὸν ἀρχέκακον πατέρα αὐτοῦ· «ὦ πλήρης παντὸς δόλου καὶ πάσης ῥᾳδιουργίας υἱὲ διαβόλου». 20.13 ἔτι δὲ καθὼς καὶ τοὺς ψευδοπρεσβύτας ἐπὶ τῆς σεμνοπρεπεστάτης Σωσάννης ἐπλήρωσεν ἀκολάστου γνώμης· ἔχει δὲ οὑτωσί· «ἦλθον δὲ καὶ οἱ δύο πρεσβύτεροι πλήρεις τῆς ἀνόμου ἐννοίας». 20.14 Καὶ ἵνα μὴ ὄχλον πολὺν τῇ ἀκοῇ παρασκευάζωμεν, πολλὰ, ἃ λέγειν εἴχομεν εἰς τοῦτο, παρέντες, συντόμως ἐροῦμεν, ὡς εἴπερ κρατεῖ ὁ λόγος αὐτῶν οὗτος, ὥρα λοιπὸν μὴ μέγα οἴεσθαι τὸ τὴν θείαν γαληνότητα οἰκεῖν ἐν πιστοῖς, ἀλλ' ὡς ἔν γε δὴ μόνῳ τῷ δοκεῖν τοῦτο τὴν δόξαν ἔχειν.
pass_a_gloss: [...] of God dwells in you?' And: 'do you not know that your bodies are a temple of the Holy Spirit in you, which you have from God?' 20.7 And to Ephesians: 'that he may give you according to the wealth of his glory to be strengthened with power through his Spirit into the inner man, that the Christ dwell through faith in your hearts.' 20.8 And as when the Master says in John: 'the Spirit of truth, which the world cannot receive, because it does not behold it nor know it. But you know it, because it remains beside you and will be in you.' And again: 'if anyone loves me, he will keep my word; and my Father will love him, and toward him we will come and make an abode beside him.' 20.9 And this will be more evident to the one attending, that having willed, the God Word who is able for all things both remained unchangeable and was carried in the womb by the virgin. 20.10 And they again stand against, contradicting: 'it is written, forsooth, about Ananias: “why did Satan fill your heart?”, and about Judas, that “Satan entered into him”.' 20.11 Toward whom it must be said that, not being partaken of nor as it were embarking on the soul, but deceiving, and working in evil counsels and a shifty way, and making [him] a by-work of his own wickedness, he fills the one not heeding the [word]: 'do not give your foot into shaking, and the one guarding you will by no means slumber.' 20.12 In the manner in which he filled Elymas his son with the suggestion of a satanic act. For Paul says to him, who happened to be foul in mind and acts and was full of the devilish villainy and was using sophistry against the saints, so as to seem that his evil-originating father dwelt in him: 'O full of all deceit and all villainy, son of the devil.' 20.13 And further, just as he also filled the false elders, in the case of the most modest Susanna, with a licentious mind; and it runs thus: 'and the two elders came, full of the lawless notion.' 20.14 And that we may not prepare a great crowd for the hearing, having let go many things which we had to say toward this, briefly we will say that, if indeed this argument of theirs prevails, it is the hour henceforth not to think it great that the divine serenity dwells in believers, but as having this repute indeed in seeming alone.
pass_b_english: … God dwells in you?” (1 Corinthians 3:16). And: “Do you not know that your bodies are a temple of the Holy Spirit within you, whom you have from God?” (1 Corinthians 6:19). And to the Ephesians: “That he may grant you, according to the riches of his glory, to be strengthened with power through his Spirit in the inner man, so that Christ may dwell in your hearts through faith” (Ephesians 3:16-17).

And it is as when the Master says in John: “The Spirit of truth, whom the world cannot receive, because it neither sees him nor knows him. But you know him, because he remains with you and will be in you” (John 14:17). And again: “If anyone loves me, he will keep my word; and my Father will love him, and we will come to him and make our dwelling with him” (John 14:23).
This will be still plainer to anyone who considers that God the Word, who can do all things, by his own will both remained unchangeable and was carried in the womb by the Virgin.

But they rise up again to object, with a show of reason: “It is written of Ananias, ‘Why has Satan filled your heart?’ (Acts 5:3), and of Judas, that ‘Satan entered into him’ (Luke 22:3; John 13:27).”

To them we must answer that Satan is not shared in, nor does he board the soul, as it were, and ride in it. He fills the one who does not heed the word, “Do not give your foot to be shaken, and he who guards you will not slumber” (Psalm 121:3), by deceiving him, by working evil counsels and a shifty character into him, and by making him a mere by-work of his own wickedness.

In this way he filled Elymas, his son, with the prompting to a satanic deed. For Paul says to him, a man foul in mind and in deeds, brimming with the devil’s villainy and using sophistry against the saints, so that his father, the author of evil, seemed to dwell in him: “O full of all deceit and all villainy, son of the devil!” (Acts 13:10).
So too he filled the false elders, in the matter of the most modest Susanna, with a licentious mind. The text runs: “And the two elders came, full of their lawless intent” (Susanna 1:28).

And so as not to weary the ear with a great crowd of words, we will pass over much that we could say on this point and put it briefly: if this argument of theirs holds, it is time to stop thinking it a great thing that the divine Serenity dwells in the faithful, and to suppose instead that this has its glory in mere appearance.

choices.issue: Workroom title, paragraphs dropped, clauses garbled
choices.choice: Retranslated the whole section from the Greek. The old row was titled 'Unit 6 rem close'; it broke off in 20.12 at 'as it seems […]', dropping the rest of 20.12 (Paul's words to Elymas, Acts 13:10), all of 20.13 (Satan filling the elders against Susanna, Susanna 28) and all of 20.14 (Didymus' conclusion that on their argument the divine indwelling would be mere appearance). In 20.11 it set the Psalm line before the description of Satan's work and called πάρεργον 'a mere side-show'. References: '(1 Cor 3:16; 6:19)' split onto the two quotations and written in full; '(Eph 3:16-17)' written in full; Luke 22:3 added beside John 13:27 (both say Satan entered Judas); Acts 13:10 and Susanna 1:28 added; '(Psalm 121:3; LXX 120:3)' given as Psalm 121:3.

choices.why: The section opens inside 1 Corinthians 3:16, begun at the end of the previous section ('the Spirit of …'); only these words are translated, with a leading ellipsis.
Didymus' ironic particle marks the objection as only apparently sound; it is his comment on the objectors, so it stands outside their quoted words.

choices.term: οὐ μετεχόμενος οὐδὲ τῇ ψυχῇ ὥσπερ ἐπιβατεύων
choices.english: Satan is not shared in, nor does he board the soul, as it were, and ride in it
choices.why: ἐπιβατεύω is to embark on or ride upon (a ship); 'as it were' keeps Didymus' ὥσπερ. The subject (Satan, from 20.10) is named for clarity.

choices.term: πληροῖ τὸν μὴ προσέχοντα τῷ. «μὴ δῴης …»
choices.english: He fills the one who does not heed the word, “Do not give your foot to be shaken …”
choices.why: The article τῷ introduces the quoted line; the stray full stop after it in the copy-text is ignored. English needs 'the word' for the article; not bracketed.

choices.english: making him a mere by-work of his own wickedness
choices.why: πάρεργον is a secondary product; the point is that the person becomes an outgrowth of Satan's wickedness, not a vessel of his substance. The object 'him' is understood from τὸν μὴ προσέχοντα.
Didymus anticipates 'son of the devil' in Acts 13:10.
An honorific periphrasis for God, like a court title; capitalized as a divine name.

choices.english: weary the ear with a great crowd of words
choices.why: Keeps Didymus' image of a 'crowd' laid on the hearing.

choices.term: «ἦλθον δὲ καὶ οἱ δύο πρεσβύτεροι πλήρεις τῆς ἀνόμου ἐννοίας»
choices.why: Didymus quotes the Theodotion text of Susanna 28; cited chapter 1 as the corpus does (e.g. Susanna 1:56 in Didymus on Zechariah).
